# Design rules

For any change a person can see. Backend-only work skips this file.

Values live in `.sdd/design-system.md` and the token location it names; this file
says how to use them. Contract status: <draft | approved>. Draft → anything the
work needs from *Pending* is an assumption labelled `pending design decision`,
never presented as approved.

§ 3–8 start as a baseline and are part of the proposal the user confirms. A rule
changed or added for this product cites its decision: `(D<n>)`.

## 1 — Pick the pattern, then the components

1. Name the surface (`design-system.md` § Product) and the screen pattern
   (§ Screen patterns) the change belongs to. None fits → it is an exception (§ 9).
2. For each piece of UI, look in § Components first, then search the UI layers.
   Use the variant that exists; do not restyle it at the call site.
3. § Proposed components are not code. Never import one; creating it is planned
   work with its own `Files` row.

## 2 — Reuse or create

- Reuse when an existing component covers the need through its parameters or
  variants.
- Add a variant to an existing component when the difference is visual only and
  the component's own file is in the plan.
- Create a component only when nothing covers the need. It uses tokens only, lives
  where its layer rule says, and is added to § Components in the same change.
- Never copy a component to change it. Two implementations of one role is how
  § Inconsistencies grows.

## 3 — Tokens

- UI code uses tokens for color, font, spacing, size, radius and shadow. No raw
  `#hex`, `rgb()`, `hsl()`, pixel size or font size outside the token location.
  Allowed literals: `0`, `100%`, `auto`, `inherit`, `currentColor`, `1px` borders.
- No token for the need → use the nearest one and note it, or raise an exception
  (§ 9). Never invent a value inline.
- A token marked `to implement` is not usable yet. Creating it is planned work.
- Color never carries meaning alone: a status also has text or an icon.

## 4 — States

Every view or component that loads, submits or can fail renders all that apply:

| State | Must |
| --- | --- |
| Loading | Content area: placeholder in the final layout, no layout jump when data lands. Action: the triggering control shows progress and ignores repeat clicks |
| Empty | Says what is missing and offers the next action. "No data yet" and "no results for these filters" differ — the second offers to clear filters |
| Error | Field error next to the field, in text, linked to it for assistive tech. Section or page error says what failed and offers retry. Input already typed is never lost |
| Success | Saving confirms without blocking (inline or toast). Creating leads to the created thing or confirms where it went |
| Disabled | Uses the disabled role and the control's native disabled state. When the reason is not obvious — permissions, missing prerequisite — it is shown in text |

## 5 — Forms, navigation, actions

- Every field has a visible label; a placeholder is never the label. Required or
  optional is marked, whichever is rarer.
- Validate on submit, then on change for fields already shown as invalid. Keep
  submit enabled; show the errors instead of silently refusing.
- One primary action per view or dialog, styled `primary`. Destructive actions use
  `danger` and ask for confirmation naming what will be lost.
- Navigation follows the surface's pattern and always shows where the user is.
- <Project-specific rules from the interview: permission handling, bulk actions,
  density, primary-action placement.>

## 6 — Responsive

- Supported widths per surface come from § Responsive. Check each change at the
  narrowest supported width, a tablet width, and a desktop width.
- No horizontal page scroll at the narrowest width. A wide table scrolls inside its
  own container.
- Touch targets on phone surfaces: at least 44×44 px.

## 7 — Keyboard and focus

- Every interactive element is reachable with Tab, in visual order, and works with
  Enter or Space. A clickable non-button element is a bug.
- Focus is always visible, using the `focus` role.
- A dialog moves focus inside on open, keeps it there, closes on Esc, and returns
  focus to what opened it.

## 8 — Verify

Report each check as met, not met, or not checked — never claim one you did not
run.

- [ ] The diff adds no raw color, size or font value outside the token location.
- [ ] Every component used exists in § Components or is created in this change and
      added there.
- [ ] Every state from § 4 that applies renders, and was seen.
- [ ] Tab order, visible focus and Esc behave per § 7.
- [ ] Narrowest, tablet and desktop widths checked; no horizontal page scroll.
- [ ] Each supported theme checked; text contrast 4.5:1, UI and focus 3:1.

## 9 — Exceptions and extending the system

- An exception — a value, component or pattern the contract does not cover — is a
  plan `Decisions` row with the reason and the alternative rejected. Approving the
  plan approves the exception for that change only.
- Making it permanent updates `.sdd/design-system.md` in the same change, listed in
  the plan's `Docs impact`: the new component in § Components with its path, a new
  value in § Tokens with source `user` and the plan as reference.
- A change to identity — palette, fonts, density, themes — is not an exception.
  It goes through `/shipit:design-system`.
